title: fix: accept empty Hermes MCP server sections
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16291

- Accept bare/explicit-null Hermes `mcp_servers` sections as empty tables while retaining rejection of scalar/list configurations.
- Convert the null YAML node to a mapping only when entries change, preserving its comments and leaving empty removal byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Extend the existing Hermes client tests for install/removal, empty-operation preservation, null-node comments, unrelated settings and invalid-table controls.

Validation: four null-table regressions fail on baseline; all 293 CLI tests pass after the fix. Build, scoped Biome and diff checks pass; strict TypeScript retains the same 35 baseline diagnostics. Independent review: both this fix and the Claude config-directory patch apply together; all 58 combined client/parent checks pass. Local tests use temporary configs, synthetic keys, Node 24 and compatible cached dependencies. Full Hermes startup was not exercised.

gist.headline: An empty table is fine
gist.blurb: Hermes MCP setup makes room for an empty `mcp_servers` section. Even the comments get to stay where they are.
gist.summary: Polli CLI accepts bare or explicit-null Hermes `mcp_servers` sections as empty tables, converting the YAML node to a mapping only when adding an entry while preserving comments.
gist.impact: Hermes users can install MCP servers into empty sections without a config error; removing from an unchanged empty section leaves the file byte-for-byte intact, while scalar and list values remain rejected.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a Hermes YAML configuration as a small blank garden plot labeled mcp_servers: Polli gently plants an MCP server entry, while a nearby comment remains undisturbed. Hermes is represented by its config, not an invented mascot.
